findings.element: 2026 Forecast Scenarios — Institution Comparison table (Key View column)
findings.detail: The 'Key View' column contains dense multi-line text at a font size that is effectively unreadable at dashboard resolution. Several cells (e.g., Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BCA Research) contain 4–6 lines of small body copy that cannot be parsed without zooming in significantly, making this unsuitable for a board-level presentation.

findings.element: Sector tiles — commentary text blocks (all 12 sector panels)
findings.detail: Each sector tile (Passenger Airlines, Hotels & Accommodations, Restaurants & Food Svcs, etc.) contains 3–4 lines of body commentary rendered at an extremely small font size. The text is illegible without zooming and would be unreadable in a printed board deck.

findings.element: Key 2025 Actuals & 2026 Macro Themes — bullet body text
findings.detail: The five numbered bullet points at the bottom of the tab contain dense paragraph-length text at a very small size. While the section headers are readable, the supporting body sentences are below a legible threshold for a CEO-level audience.

findings.element: 2025 Quarterly GDP — BEA Estimates bar chart (x-axis label)
findings.detail: The rightmost x-axis label ('2/Q1 2025' or similar) appears partially cut off at the right edge of the chart container, preventing full readability of the quarter designation.

findings.element: 2024 vs 2025 vs 2026F — Key Macro Indicators grouped bar chart (x-axis labels)
findings.detail: The x-axis category labels (REAL GDP, UNEMPLOYMENT, WAGES, CPI, FISCAL RESERVE, RATES, 2026F CONS. FUNDS %) are tightly packed and several appear to overlap or be truncated, reducing readability at board presentation scale.

findings.element: Outlook tab — fc-note commentary block
findings.detail: The blue-bordered commentary block ('Real GDP growth of 2.0% annualized is holding above stall speed…') appears to sit between the KPI tiles and the first chart section rather than clearly preceding the first chart as the topmost content element on the tab. Depending on scroll position and layout, this may violate the requirement that the fc-note precedes the first chart.

findings.element: Key 2025 Actuals & 2026 Macro Themes — bullet #3 (Tariff drag / tax cut tailwind)
findings.detail: Bullet #3 is a run-on sentence exceeding 4 sentences in a single bullet point, violating the 2–4 sentence limit for commentary blocks. The extended length dilutes the executive-level signal.

findings.element: Sector tiles grid — bottom row vs. top row panel spacing
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the top row of sector tiles (Passenger Airlines through Software & Cloud) and the bottom row (Pharmaceuticals through Freight & Logistics) appears visibly larger than the horizontal gutters between tiles within each row, creating inconsistent inter-panel spacing relative to peer panels.

findings.element: KPI metric tiles — top row (9 tiles)
findings.detail: The 'DEBT SERVICE RATIO' tile on the far right appears slightly narrower than its peers, causing its sub-label text to wrap differently and the tile to look visually misaligned with the uniform grid of the other eight KPI cards.

findings.element: KPI tiles row — sub-labels and prior-period annotations
findings.detail: The small annotation text beneath each KPI tile (e.g., 'Prior:', range values, footnote lines) renders at what appears to be ~7–8 px, making it effectively unreadable at normal viewing distance or in a printed board deck.

findings.element: Sector panel commentary lines (all ~40 sector cards)
findings.detail: The one- to two-line commentary text at the bottom of every sector card is extremely small (estimated 6–7 px). A senior reviewer would be unable to read any of the narrative without zooming in, which is unacceptable in a board-deck context.

findings.element: Broad Sector Groups table — source footnote row
findings.detail: The sources line beneath the Broad Sector Groups table is rendered in very light gray at ~6 px, falling below any reasonable legibility threshold.

findings.element: Annual-chart data vintage / filter bar annotation
findings.detail: The gray metadata line ('ANNUAL-CHART DATA VINTAGE … REPRO CAVEATS …') directly above the sector filter pills is rendered at approximately 6 px in low-contrast gray and is illegible.

findings.element: GDP Commentary block — second sentence
findings.detail: The commentary paragraph appears to be cut off mid-thought ('…domestic demand is the linchpin and it is weakening.'). While this may be intentional, the line wraps tightly against the container edge with no visible bottom padding, risking truncation on smaller viewports.

findings.element: GDP Commentary — 'fc-note' block
findings.detail: The commentary contains hedging language ('credible path', 'could provide temporary offsets') and the phrase 'it is weakening' ends abruptly. Style guide forbids hedging filler and requires 2–4 crisp, assertive sentences; the current copy reads as qualified and tentative rather than decisive.

findings.element: Sector card grid — bottom two rows (Cruise Lines / Travel Agencies)
findings.detail: The final row contains only two sector cards (Cruise Lines, Travel Agencies) while all other rows contain five or six cards, leaving a large blank area to the right. This asymmetric trailing row creates an unfinished appearance in a board presentation.

findings.element: GDP summary KPI tiles vs. Fed Funds / 10Y Treasury tiles
findings.detail: The Fed Funds Rate and 10Y Treasury tiles in the second KPI row have noticeably more vertical whitespace above them compared to the tighter first row of nine tiles, creating inconsistent inter-row rhythm.

findings.element: Sector bar charts — quarterly bar series (all sector cards)
findings.detail: Each sector card displays multiple colored bar series (appearing to represent different years or scenarios) with no legend identifying what each color represents. A board-level reader cannot determine which bar corresponds to 2023, 2024, 2025, or forecast without a legend.

findings.element: Sector card bar charts — mixed pastel palette
findings.detail: Bar colors across sector cards vary widely (pink, teal, orange, purple, yellow, blue) with no apparent mapping to the semantic roles (confirmed, warning, critical) defined in the style guide palette. The color usage appears decorative rather than informational.
